original_test_intent: Exercise or inspect the EjectMedia capability for one VirtualMedia device, with the source ambiguously presenting an action endpoint as a Get/GET query.
original_method: After resolving the method conflict, use the advertised action contract to eject exactly one approved mounted image only when the host is not using it, monitor completion, and verify device plus host recovery without automatic retry.
manual_activity: Resolve Get/GET versus POST, identify the exact mounted image/device and consumer, confirm no active host read/install/boot dependency, and approve timing plus recovery before ejection.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: POST fits EjectMedia action semantics, but it materially changes the preserved Master GET and cannot run until method, payload, mounted image and host use are confirmed; generic revert is not an adequate recovery contract.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After authoritative action discovery and explicit approval, issue one POST to the selected device's canonical EjectMedia target, then verify ejected state and host health; on timeout inspect read-only and do not retry.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager/device EjectMedia target and 15/10 timing remain; no payload, active-use state or remount recovery is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat ejection as a host-impacting state transition with a pre-use check, one-shot POST and explicit post-state/host-health oracle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the GET/POST conflict explicit, removes log clearing, validates the actual consumer and adds timeout ambiguity plus recovery controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers ejecting one selected device; it does not validate inserting or booting from media.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Ejection can irreversibly interrupt an installer or read operation; reinsertion may not restore application state even when the same image is available.

project_override_considerations: If the project intended only action discovery, use a dedicated ActionInfo review and do not execute this row. If EjectMedia is cleanup for another case, it still requires its own target and host-use approval at execution time.
expected_evidence: Canonical action URI, schema and payload
Mounted image and sanitized source identity
Host device/boot health and unrelated-state comparison
Preserved logs with no blind retry

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and Procedure label this a Get and send GET, but the URI is an EjectMedia action and DeepSeek/GPT V2 require POST. Those methods have different observable effects and blast radii, so the discrepancy is a material source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The action contract, mounted state, host-use check, approval and recovery are identifiable prerequisites, making this REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a misleading GET from masking a host-impacting eject and adds exact consumer, timeout and recovery evidence to a one-shot action.
independent_technical_reasoning: EjectMedia is safe only relative to the current consumer state. A BMC can report an image mounted while the host is reading an installer, firmware payload or boot volume; HTTP success cannot show that ejection was harmless. The reviewer must preserve the GET/POST conflict, establish the canonical action contract and require both BMC and host pre-state. Because an uncertain POST may already have completed, retry is unsafe; state must be re-read. Reinserting the same image is not equivalent to restoring an interrupted host operation, so recovery readiness and final judgment remain engineer-owned.
